p:0.h: Iranian Khorramshahr missile strikes Ramat Gan, killing two

p:1.h: Unknown projectile strikes an oil tanker near Fujairah

p:3.h: WSJ reports Russia is sharing military intelligence with Iran, including satellite imagery

p:4.h: Israeli airstrikes in Nabatieh kill three Lebanese soldiers

p:5.h: Israeli airstrike in Al-Mawasi, Gaza, kills three including a child

p:6.h: Ecuador deploys 75,000 soldiers and police to enforce a nightly curfew

p:8.h: Bandit attack in Jibia, Katsina State, kills at least 18

p:9.h: Georgian Orthodox Patriarch Ilia II dies at 93

p:10.h: UAE's offshore Shah gas field halts operations after drone attack

p:11.h: Fire at Mexico's Dos Bocas refinery kills five

p:12.h: Argentina formally withdraws from the World Health Organization

p:13.h: Brussels court orders Étienne Davignon to stand trial over the 1961 killing of Patrice Lumumba

p:14.h: Vatican appeals court orders retrial of Cardinal Giovanni Angelo Becciu

ppl.Giovanni Angelo Becciu: Italian cardinal convicted of embezzlement in 2023

p:15.h: El Salvador's legislature approves life sentences for murder, rape and terrorism

p:16.h: Shooting at Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico kills one

p:18.h: Counterterrorism chief Joe Kent resigns in protest over the Iran war

ppl.Joe Kent: Director of the U.S. National Counterterrorism Center

p:19.h: Peru's prime minister Denisse Miralles resigns; Luis Arroyo named to replace her

p:20.h: CAF overturns 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final and awards the title to Morocco

p:21.h: Venezuela beats the United States 3–2 to win its first World Baseball Classic

strategic_conclusion: Israel's killing of Ali Larijani and the Basij commander, and Mojtaba Khamenei's rejection of de-escalation, left the Iran war without a diplomatic opening on March 17, while strikes on Gulf energy assets and shipping pushed exporters to seek routes around Hormuz. The resignation of the U.S. counterterrorism chief in protest and reports of Russian intelligence support for Iran pointed to widening political stakes. In the Americas, Ecuador's curfew deployment and the Colombia–Ecuador dispute over cross-border bombings escalated, and Argentina completed its withdrawal from the WHO.
